items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Fletcher asked me if I could come and work in . . . substitute for Don Redmond while he was gone... So I went and worked with Fletcher for maybe a week or two

ctx.x: I think the next major association we should talk about is your meeting up with Horace Henderson and the whole Wilberforce Collegians period.

I met with Horace Henderson in Pittsburgh. He came there to play. Oh, did I play with him one night? I don’t even remember. But he invited me to come join the orchestra. He thought it might even be a good opportunity for me to go to school if I was so inclined, but, of course, I couldn’t have gotten into a university at the time, because I didn’t yet even have a high school diploma, nor had I even matriculated there. But so anyway, I did join the orchestra. I went to Wilberforce and they found me lodgings on…

dormitories. No, it wasn’t a dormitory, because I had my own room. But it was on campus, and the orchestra . . . gee, shortly thereafter they left for the summer to do a summer tour. The orchestra was doing so well on these tours, and I think Horace had reason to believe that his brother Fletcher would help them do something in New York. They had already had gotten a job at a club called the Club Bamville [phonetic], which I think was around 129th Street and Lennox Avenue. So we went in there, and the guys were…

items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: Fletcher invited me in to the band to replace Don.

ctx.x: And did you ever go on the road with Horace Henderson and the Collegians?
Oh yes, yes. We went on the road. And then finally, we were getting some arrangements from Fletcher, his brother, Fletcher Henderson -- and then I
think that Fletcher arranged an engagement for the band in a place called the Club Bamville. I think, which was at 129th Street and Lenox Avenue at the time.
